newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares extend losses, volume shrinks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares extend losses, volume shrinks.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended morning losses in continued selling in thin afternoon trade on Wednesday, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed at 82,215.01, down 1,507.99 points, or 1.8 percent from Tuesday when it lost 1.14 percent following Monday's 1.03 percent rise to an all-time closing high of 84,692.20.
Traded volume fell to 14.24 trillion lira from Tuesday's 16.49 trillion and Monday's 21.52 trillion.

"The market failed in three attempts to pierce the 85,000 barrier. A volume of 25 to 30 trillion lira is needed for this. Therefore, it is possible for the index to ease to 80,000-81,000 support again this week," said Dilek Akdemir from Yatirim Finansman.

The index last tried the 85,000 mark on Monday. It had drifted lower in a week-long limited pull back after a first attemt on October 31, following a 29.3 percent rally and ten record closes in a medium-term uptrend from September 13 to October 23.

Of the 226 shares traded, losers outdid gainers by 120 to 53 and 53 were steady. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI dived 1.93 percent to 86,908.46 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF dropped 1.52 percent to 79,480.99.

Active stocks were led by largely state owned flat steel company Eregli, down 750 lira at 10,500, largely state-owed petroleum refiner Tupras, up 500 lira at 21,500 and Abana Elktromekanik, down 200 lira at 7,200. Together, they made up 21.6 percent of the total volume.
